Generate a Random Mask for a List of Sparse Matrices

getRandomMask.Rd

Creates a logical sparse matrix (lgCMatrix) with TRUE/FALSE values, aligning multiple matrices based on their unique cell names and randomly masking entries.

Usage

getRandomMask(dataList, ratio, seed = NULL)

Arguments

dataList

A list of sparse matrices (each of class dgCMatrix) to be aligned.

ratio

A numeric value (between 0 and 1) specifying the proportion of TRUE values (non-masked elements).

seed

An optional numeric value to set the random seed for reproducibility (default: NULL).

Value

A sparse logical matrix (lgCMatrix) with TRUE (non-masked) and FALSE (masked) values.

Details

This function aligns a list of sparse matrices by mapping them to a shared set of unique cells (column names). It then applies a random mask based on the specified ratio, ensuring row names are properly assigned.

Examples

library(Matrix)

# Create example sparse matrices
mat1 <- Matrix(sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 20, replace = TRUE), nrow = 4, sparse = TRUE)
colnames(mat1) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
rownames(mat1) <- paste0("R", 1:4)

mat2 <- Matrix(sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 15, replace = TRUE), nrow = 3, sparse = TRUE)
colnames(mat2) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F")
rownames(mat2) <- paste0("R", 5:7)

dataList <- list(mat1, mat2)

# Generate a random mask with 20% sparsity
mask <- getRandomMask(dataList, ratio = 0.2, seed = 42)

print(mask)
#> 7 x 6 sparse Matrix of class "lgCMatrix"
#>    A B C D E F
#> R1 | | . . | .
#> R2 . . | . . .
#> R3 . . . . . .
#> R4 . . . . . .
#> R5 | . . . . .
#> R6 . | . . . .
#> R7 . . . . . |
